title: NSGo game scene (version 4)
description: SceneDoc is the root of a versioned YAML scene document.

version.description: Version is the schema version, from MinVersion to CurrentVersion. Encode writes it back as it is.

uid.description: UID is the scene file's stable ID, which stays the same when the file is renamed or moved so the tools can find it again (see package refs); empty until a tool such as game index gives it one. When set it must be a UID as resource.NewUID returns it. Resolve keeps the UID of the scene it resolves, not its base's. Both versions accept it.

inherits.description: Inherits optionally names a base scene file by its slash-separated path from the project root, such as "scenes/enemy.scene.yaml". The scene then starts as a copy of its base and changes only what it declares: its own scalar fields, camera and tilemaps replace the base's when set, its Overrides and LayerOverrides change inherited objects and layers, and its Layers add objects to the base's layers of the same name or add new layers after them. Resolve applies it. Version 2.

name.description: Name is the scene's human-readable name.

navMesh.description: NavMesh optionally names the scene's baked navigation mesh file by its slash-separated path from the project root, such as "levels/level1.navmesh.yaml": a navbake3d file with one mesh per agent type, which the game navmesh command writes from the scene's geometry. In a scene that inherits another, a NavMesh set replaces the base's. Both versions accept it.

virtualWidth.description: VirtualWidth and VirtualHeight are the scene's virtual viewport size in points. Both must be 0 or both positive.

virtualHeight.description: VirtualWidth and VirtualHeight are the scene's virtual viewport size in points. Both must be 0 or both positive.

backgroundColor.description: BackgroundColor is an optional CSS color string parsed with core.ParseColor.

ambientColor.description: AmbientColor is an optional CSS color string parsed with core.ParseColor (for example "rgba(12, 16, 30, 0.85)" or "#0c101ed8") that sets the 2D lighting ambient darkness tint (lights2d.Scene.Ambient). Both versions accept it.

camera.description: Camera holds the default camera transform for world-space layers. Nil leaves world space untransformed.

environment.description: Environment holds 3D sky, ambient/IBL lighting, fog, tone mapping and exposure settings. Version 4.

tilemaps.description: Tilemaps defines reusable named tilemaps referenced by layers via TilemapDoc.Ref.

layerOverrides.description: LayerOverrides changes the inherited layers named by its keys; it requires Inherits. Version 2.

overrides.description: Overrides changes the inherited objects whose IDs are its keys, nested children and the objects of instanced scenes (such as "enemy_1/body") included; it requires Inherits. Version 2.

layers.description: Layers are the scene's layers, drawn lowest Order first and in slice order for equal Order. In a scene that inherits another, a layer named like one of the base's adds its objects to that layer and may set nothing else (LayerOverrides changes the layer itself), and any other layer is added after the base's layers.

connections.description: Connections connect events of the scene's objects to handlers of its objects, as Godot's connections in a .tscn file do, so a button can open a door with no Go code that wires the two. Connect binds them to the handlers a ComponentRegistry declares, and Resolve carries the connections of instanced and inherited scenes into the scene that uses them.

BoundsDoc.description: BoundsDoc is an axis-aligned rectangle in world coordinates.

x.description: X and Y are the rectangle's top-left corner.

y.description: X and Y are the rectangle's top-left corner.

width.description: Width and Height are the rectangle's size; both must be positive.

height.description: Width and Height are the rectangle's size; both must be positive.

Camera3DDoc.description: Camera3DDoc configures a 3D camera attached to an object (ObjectDoc.Camera). Its world position and orientation (looking down local -Z with +Y up) come from the object's 3D transform. Version 4.

projection.description: Projection selects ProjectionPerspective ("perspective") or ProjectionOrthographic ("orthographic"); empty defaults to perspective.

fov.description: FOV is a perspective camera's vertical field of view in degrees, in (0, 180); nil defaults to 60. Refused on orthographic cameras.

orthoHeight.description: OrthoHeight is an orthographic camera's full vertical world height; nil defaults to 10. Must be finite and positive; refused on perspective cameras.

near.description: Near is the near clip plane distance; nil defaults to 0.1. Must be finite and positive for perspective cameras, and finite for orthographic cameras.

far.description: Far is the far clip plane distance; nil defaults to 1000. Must be finite and greater than near.

current.description: Current marks this camera as the scene's active 3D camera. At most one camera in a scene may be current; when none is marked, the first 3D camera in document order is used.

CameraDoc.description: CameraDoc describes a 2D camera transform for world-space layers.

x.description: X and Y are the world coordinates centered in the virtual viewport (or mapped to the origin when virtual dimensions are 0).

y.description: X and Y are the world coordinates centered in the virtual viewport (or mapped to the origin when virtual dimensions are 0).

zoom.description: Zoom is the camera zoom factor; nil defaults to 1. Must be positive when set.

rotation.description: Rotation turns the camera clockwise in radians; world geometry rotates by -Rotation around (X, Y).

bounds.description: Bounds optionally clamps the camera view inside a world rectangle.

ConnectionDoc.description: ConnectionDoc connects an event that one object emits to a handler of another object, or of the same one (SceneDoc.Connections). Signals.Emit calls the handler each time the object emits the event.

from.description: From is the ID of the object that emits the event. In a scene that instances or inherits other scene files it may name their objects, such as "door_1/button".

event.description: Event names an event a registered component type of From's object declares (ComponentType.Events), such as "pressed", or "button.pressed" to say which component when several of the object's components declare it.

to.description: To is the ID of the object whose handler runs.

handler.description: Handler names a handler a registered component type of To's object declares (ComponentType.Handlers), such as "open", or "door.open" to say which component.

args.description: Args are values for the handler's params by name; a param left out takes its default. Each is a bool, a number or a string.

once.description: Once disconnects the connection after the first time the event fires, as Godot's one-shot connections do.

EnvironmentDoc.description: EnvironmentDoc configures a 3D scene's sky, ambient fill, image-based lighting, fog, tone mapping and exposure (SceneDoc.Environment). Version 4.

sky.description: Sky configures the background sky and IBL environment map; nil leaves the scene without a skybox.

ambientColor.description: AmbientColor is the CSS color of the uniform ambient fill light (sRGB, converted to linear light); empty defaults to "#ffffff".

ambientIntensity.description: AmbientIntensity scales the uniform ambient fill light; nil defaults to 0.25. Must be finite and non-negative.

iblIntensity.description: IBLIntensity scales diffuse spherical-harmonic and specular prefiltered image-based lighting derived from Sky; nil defaults to 1 for SkyHDR and 0 otherwise. Must be finite and non-negative.

fog.description: Fog configures 3D distance and analytical height fog; nil leaves fog disabled.

tonemapping.description: Tonemapping selects TonemapNone ("none"), TonemapReinhard ("reinhard"), TonemapACES ("aces"), TonemapNeutral ("neutral") or TonemapAgX ("agx"); empty defaults to none.

exposure.description: Exposure is the linear exposure multiplier applied before tone mapping; nil defaults to 1. Must be finite and non-negative.

FogDoc.description: FogDoc configures 3D distance and analytical exponential height fog (EnvironmentDoc.Fog). Version 4.

mode.description: Mode selects FogOff ("off"), FogLinear ("linear"), FogExp ("exp") or FogExp2 ("exp2"); empty defaults to off.

color.description: Color is the CSS color of the fog (sRGB, converted to linear light when shaded); empty defaults to "#8090a8".

start.description: Start is the world distance where FogLinear fog begins; must be finite and non-negative.

end.description: End is the world distance where FogLinear fog reaches full density; must be finite and greater than Start when Mode is FogLinear.

density.description: Density is the extinction density for FogExp and FogExp2; must be finite and non-negative.

maxOpacity.description: MaxOpacity caps the combined fog factor in (0, 1]; nil defaults to 1.

heightEnabled.description: HeightEnabled enables analytical exponential height fog along the view ray.

heightBase.description: HeightBase is the world Y reference height where height fog has full HeightDensity.

heightFalloff.description: HeightFalloff is the vertical exponential decay rate above HeightBase; must be finite and non-negative.

heightDensity.description: HeightDensity is the base extinction density of height fog at HeightBase; must be finite and non-negative.

LayerDoc.description: LayerDoc is one ordered layer in a scene.

name.description: Name uniquely identifies the layer within the scene.

space.description: Space is SpaceWorld or SpaceScreen; empty defaults to SpaceWorld.

order.description: Order sets draw order across layers: lower values draw first, ties keep document order.

visible.description: Visible controls whether the layer draws; nil defaults to true.

parallaxX.description: ParallaxX scales how fast a world-space layer scrolls horizontally relative to the camera; nil defaults to 1. Zero pins the layer horizontally against camera translation, 0.5 scrolls at half speed, and values above 1 scroll faster for foreground layers. Version 3.

parallaxY.description: ParallaxY scales how fast a world-space layer scrolls vertically relative to the camera; nil defaults to 1. Zero pins the layer vertically against camera translation, 0.5 scrolls at half speed, and values above 1 scroll faster for foreground layers. Version 3.

repeatX.description: RepeatX tiles a world-space layer horizontally across the camera's visible region using RepeatWidth (or, when RepeatWidth is 0, the layer's tilemap pixel width or the scene's virtualWidth). Version 3.

repeatY.description: RepeatY tiles a world-space layer vertically across the camera's visible region using RepeatHeight (or, when RepeatHeight is 0, the layer's tilemap pixel height or the scene's virtualHeight). Version 3.

repeatWidth.description: RepeatWidth is the horizontal repeat period in layer points when RepeatX is true; 0 uses the layer's tilemap pixel width or the scene's virtualWidth. Must be non-negative. Version 3.

repeatHeight.description: RepeatHeight is the vertical repeat period in layer points when RepeatY is true; 0 uses the layer's tilemap pixel height or the scene's virtualHeight. Must be non-negative. Version 3.

tilemap.description: Tilemap optionally attaches a tilemap (by Ref, external Source, or inline grid) drawn beneath Objects.

objects.description: Objects are the placed objects in this layer.

LayerOverride.description: LayerOverride changes an inherited layer in a scene that inherits another (SceneDoc.LayerOverrides). A field left unset keeps the base layer's value.

space.description: Space replaces the layer's space when set.

order.description: Order replaces the layer's draw order when set.

visible.description: Visible replaces the layer's visibility when set.

parallaxX.description: ParallaxX replaces the layer's horizontal parallax scroll factor when set. Version 3.

parallaxY.description: ParallaxY replaces the layer's vertical parallax scroll factor when set. Version 3.

repeatX.description: RepeatX replaces whether a world-space layer tiles horizontally across the camera's visible region when set. Version 3.

repeatY.description: RepeatY replaces whether a world-space layer tiles vertically across the camera's visible region when set. Version 3.

repeatWidth.description: RepeatWidth replaces the horizontal repeat period in layer points when set. Version 3.

repeatHeight.description: RepeatHeight replaces the vertical repeat period in layer points when set. Version 3.

tilemap.description: Tilemap replaces the layer's tilemap when set.

LightDoc.description: LightDoc configures a 3D light attached to an object (ObjectDoc.Light). Its world position and forward direction (local -Z) come from the object's 3D transform. Version 4.

kind.description: Kind selects LightDirectional ("directional"), LightPoint ("point") or LightSpot ("spot").

color.description: Color is an optional CSS color string parsed with core.ParseColor (sRGB, converted to linear light when shaded); empty defaults to white.

intensity.description: Intensity scales the light's color; nil defaults to 1. Must be finite and non-negative.

range.description: Range is the smooth distance falloff cutoff in world units for point and spot lights; 0 gives unbounded inverse-square falloff. Must be finite and non-negative; refused on directional lights when non-zero.

innerCone.description: InnerCone is a spot light's inner cone half-angle in degrees, in [0, outerCone); defaults to 0. Refused on non-spot lights when non-zero.

outerCone.description: OuterCone is a spot light's outer cone half-angle in degrees, in (0, 90]; nil defaults to 45 for spot lights. Refused on non-spot lights.

shadows.description: Shadows enables shadow casting for this light.

ObjectDoc.description: ObjectDoc is one entity or visual object placed on a layer.

id.description: ID uniquely identifies the object across the entire scene.

name.description: Name is an optional human-readable display name.

prefab.description: Prefab optionally names a prefab or archetype template.

x.description: X and Y are where the object's origin sits in its parent's space, which for a top-level object is its layer's coordinate space.

y.description: X and Y are where the object's origin sits in its parent's space, which for a top-level object is its layer's coordinate space.

posZ.description: PosZ is the optional 3D Z coordinate (depth in 3D scenes) in its parent's space, distinct from 2D draw order Z.

originX.description: OriginX and OriginY are the pivot point inside the sprite's untrimmed frame.

originY.description: OriginX and OriginY are the pivot point inside the sprite's untrimmed frame.

rotation.description: Rotation turns the object clockwise in radians about its origin in 2D space.

rotX.description: RotX, RotY, and RotZ are optional 3D Euler rotations in radians about the X, Y, and Z axes, applied in that order about fixed axes (the rotation Rz * Ry * Rx).

rotY.description: RotX, RotY, and RotZ are optional 3D Euler rotations in radians about the X, Y, and Z axes, applied in that order about fixed axes (the rotation Rz * Ry * Rx).

rotZ.description: RotX, RotY, and RotZ are optional 3D Euler rotations in radians about the X, Y, and Z axes, applied in that order about fixed axes (the rotation Rz * Ry * Rx).

scaleX.description: ScaleX, ScaleY, and ScaleZ scale the object about its origin; nil defaults to 1. Negative mirrors.

scaleY.description: ScaleX, ScaleY, and ScaleZ scale the object about its origin; nil defaults to 1. Negative mirrors.

scaleZ.description: ScaleX, ScaleY, and ScaleZ scale the object about its origin; nil defaults to 1. Negative mirrors.

depth.description: Depth is the optional 3D extent along the Z axis in world units; 0 uses a default extent.

mesh.description: Mesh optionally names the built-in primitive the object draws in 3D: "box", "sphere", "plane", "capsule" or "cylinder" (MeshPrimitives lists them, and package scenemodel builds them). It cannot be combined with Model; scale the object to size the primitive.

model.description: Model optionally names the glTF 2.0 model the object draws in 3D, a .gltf or .glb file named by its slash-separated path from the project root, such as "models/crate.glb". Without ModelNode or ModelMesh the object draws every node of the model's default scene; package scenemodel loads it through a ModelResolver. Version 2.

modelNode.description: ModelNode optionally names one node of Model, the first with that name in the file, which the object draws with its descendants in place of the whole model; the object's own transform replaces the node's. It requires Model and cannot be combined with ModelMesh. Version 2.

modelMesh.description: ModelMesh optionally names one mesh of Model, the first with that name in the file, which the object draws at its origin in place of the whole model. It requires Model and cannot be combined with ModelNode. Version 2.

gridMap.description: GridMap optionally names a 3D grid map file (*.gridmap.yaml or *.gridmap.yml) by its slash-separated path from the project root, such as "levels/dungeon.gridmap.yaml". Package scenemodel loads it and instances its tiles with world3d.GridMap.BuildInstances. It cannot be combined with Mesh or Model. Version 2.

occluder.description: Occluder optionally marks this 3D object as an occluder for render3d.OcclusionBuffer, using either its own 3D geometry (mode "model") or an explicit local-space box (mode "box"). Version 2.

flipX.description: FlipX and FlipY mirror the sprite inside its untrimmed frame box.

flipY.description: FlipX and FlipY mirror the sprite inside its untrimmed frame box.

alpha.description: Alpha is the object's opacity in [0, 1]; nil defaults to 1.

z.description: Z orders objects within the layer, children included; lower Z draws first, and ties keep document order with each parent before its children.

sprite.description: Sprite optionally binds the object to a frame in a sprite.Atlas.

material.description: Material optionally names a shared material resource file by its slash-separated path from the project root, such as "materials/stone.material.yaml". Build resolves it through a MaterialResolver; the sprite draws with the material's opacity and blend mode, so every scene that uses the file changes when it is edited. In 3D it replaces every material of the object's Model, or gives its Mesh primitive its surface (package scenemodel).

particles.description: Particles optionally binds the object to a 2D particle emitter YAML file (particles.Config) and optional sprite atlas, so Build constructs a live particles.Emitter that BuiltScene.Update steps and BuiltScene.Draw renders at the object's world transform. Version 2.

light.description: Light optionally attaches a directional, point or spot 3D light to this object, placed and aimed by its 3D transform (local -Z). Version 4.

camera.description: Camera optionally attaches a perspective or orthographic 3D camera to this object, placed and oriented by its 3D transform (looking down local -Z). Version 4.

components.description: Components holds structured component data keyed by component type name.

properties.description: Properties holds arbitrary custom metadata for gameplay scripts or editors. Encode writes a whole-number float with a decimal point (2.0), so that every value reads back with the kind it was written with.

scene.description: Scene optionally instances another scene file, named by its slash-separated path from the project root such as "scenes/enemy.scene.yaml". Resolve makes the top-level objects of every layer of that scene, in document order, this object's first children, ahead of the ones in Children, with each instanced object's ID prefixed by this object's ID and a slash ("enemy_1/body"). The instanced scene's layer settings, camera, background and virtual size do not carry over, and a scene whose layers hold a tilemap cannot be instanced. Version 2.

overrides.description: Overrides changes objects of the instanced Scene, keyed by their IDs inside that scene ("body", or "gun/barrel" for an object of a scene it instances in turn); it requires Scene. Version 2.

children.description: Children are objects attached to this one, in document order. A child's transform (X, Y, Rotation, ScaleX, ScaleY, and in 3D PosZ, RotX, RotY, RotZ, ScaleZ) is local to this object, and its alpha multiplies this object's. Children belong to their parent's layer; their IDs share the scene-wide namespace, and nesting is limited to MaxObjectDepth levels.

ObjectOverride.description: ObjectOverride changes one object of an instanced or inherited scene (ObjectDoc.Overrides, SceneDoc.Overrides). Each field set replaces the ObjectDoc field of the same name; a field left unset keeps it. Components and Properties replace the object's entries key by key and keep its other keys. An override cannot change an object's ID or children, or what it instances.

prefab.description: Prefab replaces the prefab the object names.

x.description: X replaces where the object's origin sits along x in its parent's space.

y.description: Y replaces where the object's origin sits along y in its parent's space.

posZ.description: PosZ replaces the object's 3D Z coordinate in its parent's space.

originX.description: OriginX replaces the x of the object's pivot point.

originY.description: OriginY replaces the y of the object's pivot point.

rotation.description: Rotation replaces the object's clockwise 2D rotation in radians.

rotX.description: RotX replaces the object's rotation about the x axis in 3D.

rotY.description: RotY replaces the object's rotation about the y axis in 3D.

rotZ.description: RotZ replaces the object's rotation about the z axis in 3D.

scaleX.description: ScaleX replaces the object's x scale.

scaleY.description: ScaleY replaces the object's y scale.

scaleZ.description: ScaleZ replaces the object's z scale in 3D.

depth.description: Depth replaces the object's 3D extent along the Z axis.

mesh.description: Mesh replaces the built-in 3D primitive the object draws; "" removes it, as an override that gives the object a Model in place of a primitive must.

model.description: Model replaces the glTF model the object draws, a slash-separated path from the project root.

modelNode.description: ModelNode replaces the node of the model the object draws.

modelMesh.description: ModelMesh replaces the mesh of the model the object draws.

gridMap.description: GridMap replaces the 3D grid map file the object draws, a slash-separated path from the project root; "" removes it.

occluder.description: Occluder replaces the object's 3D occluder definition.

flipX.description: FlipX replaces whether the sprite is mirrored horizontally.

flipY.description: FlipY replaces whether the sprite is mirrored vertically.

alpha.description: Alpha replaces the object's opacity, in [0, 1].

z.description: Z replaces the object's draw order within its layer.

sprite.description: Sprite replaces the atlas frame the object draws.

material.description: Material replaces the material resource file the object names, a slash-separated path from the project root.

particles.description: Particles replaces the particle emitter file and optional atlas the object runs.

light.description: Light replaces the 3D light attached to the object. Version 4.

camera.description: Camera replaces the 3D camera attached to the object. Version 4.

components.description: Components replaces the object's components key by key, keeping the others.

properties.description: Properties replaces the object's custom properties key by key, keeping the others.

OccluderDoc.description: OccluderDoc marks a 3D object as an occluder that hides objects behind it in render3d.OcclusionBuffer (ObjectDoc.Occluder). Version 2.

mode.description: Mode selects the occluder geometry: "model" (the object's own Mesh or Model) or "box" (an explicit local-space solid box).

center.description: Center is the optional local-space center [x, y, z] of a "box" occluder; nil centers it at the object's origin. Only valid when Mode is "box".

size.description: Size is the optional local-space dimensions [width, height, depth] of a "box" occluder; nil defaults to [1, 1, 1], scaled by the object's transform. When set, every axis must be positive. Only valid when Mode is "box".

doubleSided.description: DoubleSided rasterizes both front and back faces of a "model" occluder when true.

ParticlesRef.description: ParticlesRef binds an object to a versioned 2D particle emitter YAML file (particles.Config) and an optional sprite atlas for its frameNames.

file.description: File is the slash-separated path from the project root to a particle emitter YAML file, such as "fx/fire.particles.yaml".

atlas.description: Atlas optionally names the sprite.Atlas an AssetResolver looks up to resolve the emitter's frameNames.

SkyDoc.description: SkyDoc configures the 3D scene sky and IBL source (EnvironmentDoc.Sky). Version 4.

kind.description: Kind selects SkyColor ("color"), SkyGradient ("gradient") or SkyHDR ("hdr").

color.description: Color is the CSS color of a SkyColor sky; empty defaults to "#141824". Refused on other sky kinds.

zenith.description: Zenith is the upper-hemisphere CSS color of a SkyGradient sky; empty defaults to "#3d6194". Refused on other sky kinds.

horizon.description: Horizon is the horizon-band CSS color of a SkyGradient sky; empty defaults to "#a8b8c7". Refused on other sky kinds.

ground.description: Ground is the lower-hemisphere CSS color of a SkyGradient sky; empty defaults to "#2b2b2e". Refused on other sky kinds.

hdr.description: HDR is the slash-separated path from the project root to an equirectangular Radiance .hdr or .pic panorama for a SkyHDR sky, such as "env/studio.hdr". Required for SkyHDR and refused on other sky kinds.

SpriteRef.description: SpriteRef identifies one frame inside a named sprite.Atlas.

atlas.description: Atlas names the sprite.Atlas an AssetResolver looks up.

frame.description: Frame names the frame inside the atlas.

TileLayerDoc.description: TileLayerDoc is one named layer of tiles of a layered grid (TilemapDoc.TileLayers), the text counterpart of one of Godot's TileMapLayer nodes.

name.description: Name identifies the layer within its tilemap; tilemap.Tilemap.Layer finds it by this name once built.

visible.description: Visible controls whether the layer draws; nil defaults to true.

opacity.description: Opacity is the layer's opacity in [0, 1]; nil defaults to 1.

rows.description: Rows are the layer's Height rows from the top, each Width cells separated by spaces. A cell is "." when empty, or the local ID of a tile of the tileset (0, 1, ...) followed by any of h, v and d to flip it horizontally, vertically or across its diagonal, as Tiled's flip bits do: "3", "3h" and "3hvd". Encode writes the cells separated by single spaces with the letters in the order h, v, d.

TilemapDoc.description: TilemapDoc describes a tilemap in one of three modes: a reference to a named top-level tilemap (Ref), an external Tiled or LDtk map (Source), or an inline grid. An inline grid is either a single grid of atlas frame numbers (Tileset and Data) or, in version 2, a layered grid that places the tiles of a YAML tileset (TilesetFile and TileLayers).

ref.description: Ref names an entry in SceneDoc.Tilemaps. Only valid on a layer's Tilemap.

source.description: Source is the slash-separated path from the project root of an external map: a Tiled map (.tmj or .tmx) or an LDtk project (.ldtk). Build loads it itself when its resolver implements FileResolver, as FSAssets does, or through a TilemapResolver.

level.description: Level names the level of an LDtk Source to build; empty builds the project's first level. It requires a .ldtk Source. Build reads a source with a Level through a FileResolver even when the resolver implements TilemapResolver. Version 2.

offsetX.description: OffsetX and OffsetY shift the tilemap's top-left corner (cell 0, 0) in its layer's coordinate space in points. Version 3.

offsetY.description: OffsetX and OffsetY shift the tilemap's top-left corner (cell 0, 0) in its layer's coordinate space in points. Version 3.

tileWidth.description: TileWidth and TileHeight are each tile's size in points for an inline grid.

tileHeight.description: TileWidth and TileHeight are each tile's size in points for an inline grid.

width.description: Width and Height are the inline grid dimensions in tiles.

height.description: Width and Height are the inline grid dimensions in tiles.

tileset.description: Tileset is, for a single grid, the atlas name providing frames keyed by 1-based tile ID ("1", "2", ...).

tilesetFile.description: TilesetFile is, for a layered grid, the YAML tileset (*.tileset.yaml, tilemap.TilesetDoc) whose tiles the cells place, by its slash-separated path from the project root. Version 2.

data.description: Data holds a single grid's Width*Height row-major tile IDs; 0 is an empty cell.

tileLayers.description: TileLayers are a layered grid's tile layers, drawn in order, each Width by Height cells, at most MaxTileLayers of them. Version 2.
